classification.difficultyReason: Part b requires interpreting an angle south of west, converting it to a clockwise bearing and reversing direction; part d requires selecting the relevant angle despite extra triangle information.

content.prompt: Determine the true bearing of $A$ from $B$.

spec.description: North arrow at A and segment AB extending southeast; the clockwise angle from north to AB is 110 degrees.
spec.mathematics: AB has bearing 110 degrees from A. Its reverse direction has bearing 290 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 110-degree angle is visible; the requested bearing is omitted.

answer.worked:
The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $110^{\circ}$. Reverse bearings differ by $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }B&=110^{\circ}+180^{\circ}\\&=290^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: North arrow and dashed west cue at A; AB lies 20 degrees south of west.
spec.mathematics: AB has bearing 270 minus 20 equals 250 degrees from A. The reverse bearing is 070 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 20-degree angle is visible; no calculated bearing is shown.

answer.worked:
$AB$ is $20^{\circ}$ south of west.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }B\text{ from }A&=270^{\circ}-20^{\circ}\\&=250^{\circ}.\\\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }B&=250^{\circ}-180^{\circ}\\&=070^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: North arrow and east ray at B, with a right-angle square; BA extends southwest and is 135 degrees clockwise from east.
spec.mathematics: The clockwise angle from north to BA is 90 plus 135 equals 225 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: The right-angle mark and supplied 135-degree angle remain visible; the requested bearing is omitted.

answer.worked:
Measure clockwise from north at $B$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }B&=90^{\circ}+135^{\circ}\\&=225^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete isosceles triangle ABP with matching single ticks on AB and AP, 40-degree angle at A, north arrows at A and B, and a 106-degree angle west of north at B.
spec.mathematics: AB equals AP and angle BAP is 40 degrees. The counterclockwise angle from north at B to BA is 106 degrees, so the clockwise bearing is 360 minus 106 equals 254 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Both supplied angles and equal-side marks remain visible; the calculated 254-degree bearing is omitted.

answer.worked:
The bearing is measured clockwise from north at $B$. Angles at a point sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }B&=360^{\circ}-106^{\circ}\\&=254^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
